title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Top Issues Playbook (2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site publishing workflows, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is a consistent, low-friction developer onboarding experience and a single source of truth for common issues and remediation steps.

Audience:
- Developer experience engineers
- SDK authors
- Technical writers
- Solutions engineers and support

Scope:
- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go)
- Quickstarts and templates for common integration patterns
- API example standards (REST + SDK) and request/response examples
- Docs site operating procedures (pull-request flow, CI checks, releases)
- Top support issues + canonical fixes and runbook links

Standards: SDK Guides

1) Structure (required):
- Title and short description (1 sentence)
- Compatibility / prerequisites (SDK version, runtime, credentials)
- Installation (pip/npm/go get) with exact commands
- Quick hello-world code sample (SDK + REST where applicable)
- Common patterns: auth, streaming, retries, batching
- Troubleshooting section with link to support playbook
- API surface table: method, required params, return shape, SLO impact (if applicable)

2) Style: concise, example-first. Prefer copy-paste code blocks. Include both synchronous and streaming examples for generation endpoints. Always surface the CLI / curl equivalent.

3) Example: Python install + hello: 
- pip install redwood-inference
- from redwood import Client
- client = Client(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
- resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1", prompt="Hello")

Quickstarts & Templates

Purpose: Provide minimal, runnable projects that demonstrate common integrations. Quickstarts must be executable in under 5 minutes with free-tier credentials.

Required quickstart files:
- README.md with TL;DR and expected output
- 1 example script per language (python/main.py, ts/index.ts, go/main.go)
- .env.example with required env vars
- dockerfile (optional) or instructions for running locally
- LICENSE (Apache-2.0) and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (link)

Quickstart template checklist:
- Uses latest stable SDK pinned in requirements.txt/package.json/go.mod
- CI badge indicating quickstart smoke test
- Small dataset / prompt set used for testing included in /test/prompts.txt
- A smoke test in CI that runs a single short request and asserts a 200 response and non-empty body

API Examples (REST + SDK)

1) Canonical format for examples:
- Language header (e.g., ### Python)
- Copy-pasteable command or snippet
- Expected response (trimmed) and explanation of fields
- Security note: do not paste real API keys

2) Request/response conventions:
- Use consistent example model names (redwood-1, redwood-1-small)
- Use short prompts for examples, but include a comment showing a long-form variant
- For streaming: show how to handle partial events and reconnect logic

Docs Site Operating Procedures

1) Authoring workflow:
- Create a feature branch: docs/<short-desc>
- Open a PR against main with the doc .md or .json and a short description
- Include a checklist in the PR description (template below)

2) PR Checklist (required):
- Title, space, and all metadata present in JSON front-matter
- Code blocks execute locally (smoke-run)
- Accessibility check (images alt text)
- Links validated (no 404s)
- Reviewer assigned from devex team

3) CI checks (automated):
- Linter: spellcheck + style rules (max 90 chars line length for prose)
- Examples smoke tests: run language-specific smoke tests using a redwood-test API key stored in CI secrets
- Link checker: fails on 404s or dead anchors
- Security scan: flag hard-coded secrets

4) Release cadence and tagging:
- Docs deploys on merge to main (hourly incremental builds)
- Major edits (API contract changes) require a release note entry and changelog update

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (Canonical fixes should be reproducible, short, and include owner)

1) Authentication: 401 / invalid_api_key
- Symptom: 401 on every request from customer
- Root cause: API key not set or using sandbox key on production endpoint
- Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY env var present; confirm endpoint (api.redwood.com vs api-internal) and test with curl: 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/models
- Owner: solutions-engineering@redwood.com

2) Streaming disconnects / partial output
- Symptom: client gets intermittent truncated responses or connection resets
- Root cause: long-lived connections behind intermediate proxies (corporate NAT) or missing client-side reconnect logic
- Canonical fix: Use chunked streaming handler from SDK examples; enable keepalive and exponential reconnect with jitter. Reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/streaming-reconnect-patterns
- Owner: devex-runtime-team@redwood.com

3) High latency for short requests (p50 > 200ms)
- Symptom: short prompt generation reports high tail latency
- Root cause: misconfigured routing (requests pinned to low-priority region) or batching disabled for small ephemeral requests
- Canonical fix: Ensure client route header is set for region preference; for latency-sensitive flows set batching=false in request metadata; open ticket to infra if p95>1s
- Owner: eng-sre@redwood.com

4) Bad output quality after model pin/upgrade
- Symptom: regression in quality when model pinned to new version
- Root cause: model variant mismatch or missing default prompt templates
- Canonical fix: Run the evaluation harness for the impacted prompt-set; if regression confirmed, roll back to previous model via rollout policy and open model-onboarding ticket
- Owner: applied-ml@redwood.com

5) Rate limit errors (429) during burst traffic
- Symptom: clients receive 429s during short spikes
- Root cause: missing client-side exponential backoff or underestimated quota for route
- Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter in SDK; for verified customers increase quota via Dedicated allocation or negotiate burst capacity
- Owner: product-ops@redwood.com

6) SDK install failures / compatibility issues
- Symptom: pip install fails on older pip / Python versions or lockfile mismatch
- Canonical fix: Publish compatibility matrix in SDK guide; add wheel distributions for common platforms; recommend pip>=23 and show virtualenv steps; add CI job for testing against oldest supported runtimes
- Owner: devex-sdk@redwood.com

7) Embedding mismatches (vector dim mismatch)
- Symptom: application raises shape errors when persisting vectors
- Root cause: using embeddings from different model family or old dimension without migration
- Canonical fix: Validate embedding dimension in preflight check; provide migration script to re-embed corpus using redwood-embed-1; add schema version to stored vectors
- Owner: search-and-embeddings@redwood.com

8) Docs site build failures after image additions
- Symptom: docs build fails on CI with image processing error
- Root cause: images over size limit or unsupported format in markdown
- Canonical fix: Optimize images using docs-image-optimizer; convert to webp/jpeg; update docs-lint rule to check size < 2MB
- Owner: devex-docs@redwood.com

Runbooks & Escalation

- For any issue that cannot be resolved with canonical fix within 30 minutes, open an incident in PagerDuty with severity based on customer impact and follow oncall-and-incident-response/process. Link the incident to the doc page and update the doc with the new remediation steps once resolved.

Templates (copy-paste)

1) Quickstart README header:
# Quickstart: Text Generation (Python)
TL;DR: Run `python main.py` to generate a short greeting.
Prereqs: Python 3.10+, REDWOOD_API_KEY set.

2) SDK doc front-matter (JSON):
{
  "title": "Quickstart: Text Generation (Python)",
  "space": "eng-developer-experience",
  "author": "<author name>",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "draft",
  "created_at": "2026-01-01",
  "last_updated": "2026-01-01"
}

(Replace fields and move to published when verified.)

Maintenance & Ownership

- DevEx docs are owned by the Developer Experience team. Each quickstart and SDK guide must list an "owner" line in the doc body. Owners must respond to doc PR reviews within 3 business days.
- Quarterly doc audits: list of critical docs and smoke tests executed by CI. Outdated docs should be flagged with status: review_required.

Appendix: Helpful Commands
- Local smoke run (Python): `REDWOOD_API_KEY=$KEY python -c "from redwood import Client; print(Client().list_models())"`
- Curl models list: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/models`
- Link checker (local): `npx broken-link-checker http://localhost:3000`

If you have questions or want an onboarding review for a new quickstart, create a ticket in the devex-docs backlog and assign to devex-docs@redwood.com.
